observation.visible_scene: Outdoor setting in front of a dark-roofed open pavilion with bare trees and a pale sky in the background. In the foreground left, a person wearing a teal t-shirt and a red-and-grey baseball cap has their right hand pressed against the face of a second person standing center-right, who wears a black t-shirt with a yellow/red flame graphic. The pressing hand and the receiver's face are covered by a bright white powdery cloud that is bursting outward; the receiver's eyes are squeezed shut.
visible_changes: The white powder cloud is already erupting at the first frame and continues to expand and billow throughout the excerpt, growing larger, fluffier, and more diffuse toward the top, right, and rear of the receiver's head.
Individual powder particles and fine spray drift outward from the contact zone, with the densest white mass remaining around the hand and the receiver's face.
The cap-wearer's hand stays pressed against the receiver's face for the whole segment, with only minor shifts in finger/hand shape as the powder accumulates around it.
The receiver's head and torso remain essentially stationary; the dominant motion is the expansion of the powder, not translation of the people.
The background pavilion, posts, trees, and sky hold a constant position and size across all frames, indicating a static camera rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: The moment of first contact / the slap that initiated the powder burst is not shown; the burst is already in progress at t=0.
What happens after the excerpt ends (hand withdrawal, receiver reaction, cleanup) is not visible.
The exact identity of the white substance and how it got onto the hand is not established by the clip.
uncertain_details: Whether the hand applies additional pressure or simply remains in place is hard to confirm; the apparent motion is mostly the powder deforming around a fairly fixed hand.
Any very slight camera drift cannot be fully ruled out, but background evidence suggests the framing is static.
The footage appears to be slow-motion, but the playback rate is not directly observable.
